representations.name: Logarithmic exponent polytope
representations.new_information: Records alpha=r*loglog(k)/log(k), c=log(n)*loglog(k)/log(k)^2, and the leading lambda exponent as simultaneous variables.
representations.repairs_loss: Separates leading log(k)^2/loglog(k) costs from lower-order log(r!) costs.
representations.first_test: Derive every Theorem 4.1 term as a linear or fractional inequality in alpha,c and the lambda exponent.
representations.closure_interface: The feasible polytope must give both an attainable c(theta) and a dual infeasibility certificate.

representations.name: A--B multiplicative invariant
representations.new_information: Retains the exact lambda-independent identity A^(2r-1) B^(r-1)=k^(theta-1).
representations.repairs_loss: Turns the heuristic balancing of lambda into a primal--dual optimality certificate.
representations.first_test: Minimize max(A,B) and A+B over positive lambda and compare their k-exponents.
representations.closure_interface: Must prove non-balanced lambda cannot cross the same exponent threshold.

representations.name: Least admissible derivative order
representations.new_information: Keeps the exact stopping rule n*r!<=k^(r+theta) and its failed predecessor.
representations.repairs_loss: Avoids charging log(r!) at the same scale as log n.
representations.first_test: Prove r<=(c+epsilon)log(k)/loglog(k) uniformly for n in the large range.
representations.closure_interface: The upper bound must coexist with r>=3 and Theorem 4.1's derivative constraint.

representations.name: Exact residual-term ledger
representations.new_information: Tracks the third term and r*lambda using the failed predecessor inequality rather than a global coarse power.
representations.repairs_loss: Distinguishes genuine frontier constraints from harmless bounded-r and polylogarithmic factors.
representations.first_test: Maximize the exact exponent h_theta(r)=(2-theta-(1-theta)(2r-1)/(3r-2))/r for r>=3.
representations.closure_interface: Must show both residual terms are o(k^theta/log k) on the proposed full c-range.

representations.name: Comparable shifted prime blocks
representations.new_information: Represents each base x in [k,2k] with x asymptotic to k and a length comparable to k^theta.
representations.repairs_loss: Tests whether extra prime supply can outweigh repeated Konyagin errors.
representations.first_test: Normalize each block's prime count and A--B product and sum over finitely or polylogarithmically many blocks.
representations.closure_interface: An improvement requires a smaller average normalized error, not merely more blocks.

representations.name: Variable-length block exponent
representations.new_information: Uses a block length k^beta and the matching divisibility threshold k^(beta-1).
representations.repairs_loss: Exposes the tradeoff between prime availability and the Konyagin product exponent 1-beta.
representations.first_test: Optimize beta subject to a proved prime count at that scale.
representations.closure_interface: A better frontier requires beta<theta with a valid prime input or a theorem not based on independent block counts.

representations.name: Range-interface atlas
representations.new_information: Keeps the small, medium, medium-large and large n interfaces with their exact theta assumptions and output interval.
representations.repairs_loss: Prevents a large-n optimization from silently changing theta quantifiers or the final prime interval.
representations.first_test: Replay every source-paper range with symbolic theta and locate the strongest condition outside Section 6.
representations.closure_interface: Must finish first in (k,k+3k^theta) and only then embed this interval into (k,2k).

representations.name: Termwise-certificate dual barrier
representations.new_information: Defines the exact proof class: nonnegative blockwise Theorem 4.1 upper bounds followed by an asymptotic little-o comparison with short-interval prime counts.
representations.repairs_loss: Prevents a no-go result about a proof certificate from being misstated as a lower bound on the true bad set.
representations.first_test: Construct the dual inequalities r>=c log(k)/loglog(k) and (3r-2)loglog(k)<=(1-theta)log(k).
representations.closure_interface: The two inequalities should meet at the same c(theta) as the attaining construction.
